SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.3376.543
1. (Currently amended) A method performed by an anesthetizing monitoring unit configured to generate an improved evoked electromyography response signal (XResponse), the method comprising:generating a single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) using the anesthetizing monitoring unit, wherein the single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) comprises a single pulse and is configured to stimulate a motor nerve of a patient,
outputting the generated single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) to stimulating electrodes on the patient using an output port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit,
receiving a single evoked electromyography, EMG, response signal (SResponse) from receiving electrodes on the patient at an input port of the anesthetizing monitoring unit, having a duration (TResponse), in response to the transmitted stimuli signal (Sstimuii),
estimating a periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), having the duration (TResponse), by using temporal segments of based on a noise signal (SNoise) by splitting the noise signal (SNoise) into temporal segments,wherein:the noise signal (SNoise) is caused by an electric power grid having a frequency;the temporal segments each have a periodic duration (TPeriodic) matching the frequency of the electric power grid; andSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.150.727 temporal segments of the noise signal (SNoise) used during the estimating of the periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic)-are detected during a time interval (TNoise) not overlapping with a stimuli signal interval (Tstimulus) of the single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) and not overlapping with the duration of the response signal (TResponse),generating the improved response signal SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.693 by subtracting the noise waveform from the response signal (SResponse) to reduce noise in the response signal (SResponse) caused by the electric power grid,storing the improved response signal SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.697 in a memory in the anesthetizing monitoring unit, andpresenting the improved response signal SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.697 on a display in the anesthetizing monitoring unit.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.376.543
2. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 1, wherein the step of estimating the periodic noise waveform further comprises:
splitting the noise signal (SNoise) into a number N of temporal segments (Si, S2, ..., SN),
generating a periodic noise template (STemplate) by aggregating the N temporal segments (Si, S2, ..., SN),
wherein the periodic noise waveform (SPeriodic), isestimated by subsequently repeating the periodic noise template (STemplate) N times.
3. (Original) The method according to claim 2, wherein the periodic noise template (STemplate) is generated by averaging discrete samples over the N temporal segments (Si, S2, ..., SN).
4. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 1, wherein the method further comprises determining an anesthetized patient state by determining a neuromuscular function value using properties of the improved response signal
5. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 1, wherein the anesthetized patient state is a selection of any of "insufficient anesthetic level", "low anesthetic level", "sufficient anesthetic level", "normal breathing function", "capable of sustaining breathing" or "in need of ventilator".SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.733
6. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 4, wherein the properties of the improved response signal (XResponse) include amplitude value/s(AResponse') and wherein the neuromuscular function value is determined by comparing a quota of amplitude value/s of the improved response signal (XResponse) and additional amplitude value/s to a set of predetermined amplitude value/s thresholds, wherein the additional amplitude values are selected from amplitude value/s of the stimuli signal (SstimuSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.157 and historical amplitude value/s of the improved response signal (XResponse).
7. (Cancelled).SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.376.543
8. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 2, wherein the temporal segments (Si, S2, ..., SN) have a duration (TPeriodic) proportional to the noise signal (SNoise).
9. (Original) The method according to claim 8, wherein the duration (TPeriodic) is selected using a strongest periodic noise component of the noise signal (SNoise).
10. (Previously Presented) An anesthetizing monitoring unit configured to generating an improved evoked electromyography response signal (XResponse), the anesthetizing monitoring unit comprising:
an input port,
an output port, and
processing circuitry being configured to perform the method according to claim 1.
11. (Previously Presented) An anesthetizing monitoring system configured to determine an anesthetized patient state, the anesthetizing monitoring unit comprising:
an anesthetizing monitoring unit comprising an input port and an output port,stimulating electrodes electrically coupled to the output port and being configured to receive a stimuli signal (Sstimuli) from the output port and deliver the stimuli signal (SstimuSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.157 to the anesthetized patient,SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.160.157
receiving electrodes electrically coupled to the input port and being configured to obtain an evoked electromyography, EMG, response signal (SResponse), in response to the stimuli signal (Sstimu and a noise signal (SNoise), from the anesthetized patient, the anesthetizing monitoring unit being configured to perform the method according to claim 1.
12. (Previously Presented) A computer program is provided comprising computer-executable instructions for causing an anesthetizing monitoring unit, when theSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.3376.543computer-executable instructions are executed on a processing unit comprised in the anesthetizing monitoring unit, to perform the method according claim 1.
13. (Original) A computer program product comprising a computer-readable storage medium, the computer-readable storage medium having the computer program according to claim 12 embodied therein.
14. (Original) A carrier comprising the computer program according to claim 12, wherein the carrier is one of an electronic signal, optical signal, radio signal, or computer readable storage medium.
15. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 6, wherein the threshold values are predetermined properties of historical improved response signals received at the anesthetizing monitoring unit prior to the response signal (SResponse) being received by the anesthetizing monitoring unit, wherein the threshold values are stored in the memory of the anesthetizing monitoring unit.
16. (Previously Presented) The method according to claim 1, wherein the temporal segments of the noise signal (SNoise) are gathered by the anesthetizing monitoring unit within an adjacent time interval (TNoise) not overlapping with a stimuli signal interval (Tstimulus) and the duration of the response signal (TResponse).
